question: Watt-Evans gets by on an estimated 200 true fans, well below 1,000. What explains this in Kelly's account?
options: His publisher advances, backed by many lesser fans, supplement the fan income
His fans pay through a label, which raises the revenue he keeps per fan
His fans each spend several times the $100 average and he has almost no costs
He releases a single chapter a year, so few buyers are needed to cover it

private.explanation: The 1,000 figure assumes true fans are the whole income. Mixing in traditional publishing means fewer are needed, which also shows the approach is not exclusive.
option_explanations: Right: Kelly says he also publishes traditionally, with advances backed by thousands of lesser fans, so true fans are only part of his income.
Direct payment is the model here; intermediaries would lower per-fan revenue.
The essay gives no such figures for his prices or costs.
Chapters were posted as each $100 goal was reached, not once a year.
